Version 2.0.0

dAVEBOx SA

User manual · version 2.0.0

dAVEBOx is an 8-track sequencer and sampler for Ableton Move. It records, arranges and plays back notes and automation. Each track plays one of Move's own instruments, a Schwung effect chain, an external synth on the USB-A port, or samples of its own on an Audio or Slicer track.

dAVEBOx runs inside Schwung and takes over Move's pads, knobs and screen while it is open. It uses Move's vocabulary of tracks and clips, and Coming from Move sums up what carries over and what is different.

If you are new to dAVEBOx, start with the Quick Start. It takes about fifteen minutes to go from a new project to a looping pattern with effects and scenes. This manual is the full reference.

Video

Seven short videos walk through dAVEBOx on a real Move. Watch the whole playlist, or start with the four-minute showcase. Sections of this manual that a video covers link to the moment it starts.

1

Overview

1.1How a Project Is Built

  • A note, or an automation point, sits on a step: one slot of a clip's grid.
  • A run of steps makes a clip, which also carries its own sequencer effects and automation. An Audio clip plays a sample instead of steps of notes.
  • A track holds 16 clips, and only one of them plays at a time. An Audio track has a sample in each clip, and a Slicer track has one sample that its clips play in slices.
  • A scene is one clip from each of the 8 tracks, launched together.
  • The whole thing is saved as a dAVEBOx project. See Projects.

Tracks and clips are the same objects as on Move; scenes are dAVEBOx's own. dAVEBOx replaces Move's sequencer, not its instruments.

1.2The Two Views

VideoTutorial 1.1: Two views

[Note/Session] switches between the two views (see Switching Views).

Track ViewSession View
ForBuilding one clip in detailLaunching and arranging clips
PadsPlay notes or drum lanesThe clip grid
StepsThe clip's stepsLaunch scenes

1.3Five Kinds of Track

TypeHow it works
MelodicScale-snapped notes on the pads and steps. See Melodic Clips
DrumThe pads become 32 drum lanes, each its own step sequence. See Drum Clips
AudioEach clip plays its own sample, in time with the project. See Audio Tracks
SlicerOne sample for the track, cut into slices you play and sequence from the pads. See Slicer Tracks
ConductorPlays no notes of its own; it transposes the other tracks live. See The Conductor

1.4Coming from Move

Most of Move's gestures work here as they do on Move, including:

  • Placing notes: press a pad and then a step, or hold a step and press pads.
  • [Loop]: hold it to see the clip's pages on the step buttons, and turn the jog while holding it to change the length.
  • Automation: turn a knob while recording. To switch a knob's automation off, hold [Mute] and touch the knob; to clear it, hold [Delete] and touch it. To set a value for one step, hold the step and turn a knob. Holding [Mute] lights automated knobs red.
  • Most [Shift] + Step shortcuts: [Step 1] opens your projects, 2 settings, 5 tempo, 6 the metronome, 7 groove, 9 key and scale, 10 fixed velocity, 11 the arpeggiator, 15 doubles the loop and 16 quantizes.

Where dAVEBOx differs:

On MoveIn dAVEBOx
There are 4 tracks, chosen with the track buttons.There are 8 tracks. Tracks 1–4 play Move's instruments and tracks 5–8 Schwung instruments. To choose one, hold [Shift] and turn the jog, or hold the jog and press [Step 1–8]. See Selecting a track.
The buttons left of the pads select tracks.The side buttons launch the track's clips in Track View, and scenes in Session View.
Session Mode has a row per track, a column per scene and 8 clips per track.Session View has a column per track, a row per scene and 16 clips per track. It shows 4 rows at a time; [+] and [−] scroll. See Session View.
You slide a finger down a column to play a scene.You press a side button or a step button to launch a scene. See Scenes.
The knobs play the selected device, and the jog picks the device.The knobs play a bank: clip settings, sequencer effects, sound, macros or automation. The jog's bank map picks the bank. See Banks and the Bank Map.
When you hold a step, the jog sets length and Volume sets velocity.When you hold a step, the knobs set pitch, length, velocity, nudge and more. See Editing notes.
You browse a track's presets with the jog.On a Move track, you open Move's own editor from the track's menu and browse there. See Choosing a track's sound.
[Mute] and a track button mutes a track; add [Shift] to solo.In Track View, press [Mute], or hold [Shift] and press [Mute]. In Session View, hold [Mute] and touch a track's knob. See Mute and solo in Session View.
You hold a track button and turn Volume to set its level.Hold [Shift] and turn the Volume knob to set the active track's volume. In Session View the knobs are a mixer.
[Shift] + [Step 8] turns on 16 Pitches for a drum track.[Shift] + [Step 8] switches the right-hand pads between velocity zones and Note Repeat. See Drum Clips.

1.5dAVEBOx SA and Schwung

dAVEBOx SA runs as its own session. You start it from Schwung (see Open dAVEBOx), and Move restarts into the sequencer, on a fork of the Schwung host that plays the modules, presets and samples installed in your Schwung. It needs Schwung installed and does not replace it.

  • A reboot returns you to official Schwung, unless you made dAVEBOx your boot default.
  • Samples, presets and modules are shared between the two, but settings are not. See dAVEBOx and official Schwung.
  • Your Move Sets are not shared. dAVEBOx keeps its own projects.

An earlier form of dAVEBOx runs as an ordinary tool inside official Schwung and is described in MANUAL.md. It still works but is no longer developed. It has 2 insert effects per chain instead of 4 and no send effect buses, where dAVEBOx SA has two (A and B).

2

Getting Started

2.1Install and Remove

dAVEBOx SA needs Schwung 1.7.3 or newer. To install it:

  1. In a browser, open Schwung's web manager at move.local:7700 and go to Modules. Plain move.local is Ableton's own Move Manager.
  2. Find dAVEBOx SA in the catalog, under Tools, and click Install.
  3. On the Move, open dAVEBOx SA. The first launch finishes installing by itself in about a minute.

Updates arrive the same way, and your projects carry over.

If dAVEBOx SA isn't in your catalog yet, download davebox-sa-module.tar.gz from its release page, then in Modules open Install Custom Module, choose the file under From Tarball, and click Install from File.

To remove dAVEBOx SA, install davebox-uninstall-module.tar.gz from the release page the same way, quit dAVEBOx, and choose Uninstall dAVEBOx SA in Schwung's tool menu. Your projects and settings stay in /data/UserData/daveboxSA, so a later install picks them up.

2.2Open dAVEBOx

Hold [Shift] and press [Step 13] (the star) to open Schwung's tool menu, then choose dAVEBOx SA and confirm. Move restarts under the dAVEBOx host, which takes a few seconds, and you land on the project picker, with one pad per project.

To load the project you had open last, click the jog. To start a new project, hold [Shift] and tap an empty pad. To load another project, hold [Shift] and tap its pad. See The Project Picker.

To leave dAVEBOx from anywhere, hold [Shift] and press [Back]; it saves first. See Saving, Suspending and Leaving.

You can also open dAVEBOx at power-on. While the screen reads "Loading Schwung — press [Back] to change", hold [Back], turn the jog to dAVEBOx SA and click the jog. Picking a row in that boot menu also makes it your default for the next power-on; to change back, hold [Back] at power-on and pick Schwung. Leaving dAVEBOx always returns you to Schwung.

2.3Nothing to Set Up

Every new project is ready to play. Tracks 1–4 play Move's four instruments, loaded with a random stock drum kit, a bass and two polyphonic sounds, like a new Move Set. Track 1 is a drum track. Tracks 5–8 stay silent until you choose a sound for them.

Tracks that play Move instruments need Move's Link setting. dAVEBOx turns Link on each time it starts, set to Tempo with start/stop sync off. If you turn it off in Move Settings, it stays off until the next session, and dAVEBOx warns you while it is off.

The Quick Start walks you through a first pattern.

Quick Start

A hands-on walkthrough that takes you from a new project to a looping pattern with effects, scenes, and a taste of Performance Mode — in about fifteen minutes.

Work through the lessons in order. Each one builds on the last. When you want the full detail on anything you meet here, the dAVEBOx SA Manual is the complete reference — this guide links into it as you go.

Before you start: open a project

There is nothing to set up. Every dAVEBOx project is created ready to play: tracks 1–4 play Move's four instruments — a random drum kit, a bass and two polyphonic sounds, like a new Move set — and tracks 5–8 each have a Schwung chain of their own. dAVEBOx turns Move's Link on by itself each time it starts.

  1. Open Schwung's tool menu (Shift + Step 13 — the star) and choose dAVEBOx SA. The screen goes dark for a few seconds while Move restarts; that pause is the startup, and nothing has gone wrong.
  2. You land on the project picker. dAVEBOx keeps its own projects, separate from your Move sets — one pad per project. Nothing is open yet.
  3. Hold Shift and tap an empty pad. That creates a new project and opens it in one press — if you have project templates, it asks Empty or Template first. (Later, to carry on where you left off, just click the jog jog: the project you last had open is already selected.)

You can come back to the picker at any time with Shift + Step 1. More in the manual's Projects section.

A two-minute tour

dAVEBOx has two views, and you switch between them with the Note/Session button:

  • Session View (where you start) — a grid of clips. Each column is a track, each row is a scene. This is where you launch and arrange clips.
  • Track View — the detailed editor for one clip at a time: pads play notes, the 16 step buttons hold its pattern.

A few things worth knowing before the first lesson:

  • The jog wheel shows the bank map. In Track View, press and hold the jog (the clickable knob on the left): the left 4×4 pads become a map of the track's parameter banks — its effects and clip settings — and the screen shows the same map. Tap a pad to go to that bank, then let go of the jog. Letting go without tapping puts the map away without choosing.
  • There are no track buttons. While the bank map is up, Steps 1–8 are the tracks, each lit in its own colour. Tap one to switch track. Holding Shift and turning the jog also walks through the tracks.
  • Note/Session is the way home. From any menu, bank or picker, one press takes you to Session View. Holding Back returns you to the overview of the view you're in.
  • Two menus: Shift + Step 2 opens Project Settings (tempo, key, scale, saving and leaving). The active track's TRACK CONFIG menu (its instrument, effects and settings) is the CONFIG pad on the bank map — the bottom-left pad.

That's enough to begin.

Lesson 1 — Your first drum beat

Track 1 of a new project is already a drum track, playing a Move drum kit.

  1. Tap Note/Session to switch into Track View, on track 1.

The pad grid is split. The left 4×4 pads are drum lanes — one drum sound each. The right 4×4 sets the velocity of the hits you place; you can ignore it for now.

  1. Tap a few of the left pads. You'll hear each lane's sound, and the last one you tap becomes the selected lane.
  2. With a lane selected, tap step buttons 1–16 (the row below the pads) to place hits. Try steps 1, 5, 9, and 13 for a steady pulse.
  3. Select a different lane pad and place a different rhythm — a snare on 5 and 13, a hat on every step.
  4. Press Play. Your beat loops.

Each lane is its own little sequencer, so you can even give them different lengths later for polyrhythms. Full detail lives in the manual's Drum Clips chapter.

Lesson 2 — Add a melodic part

Now let's play some notes on another track.

  1. Hold the jog, tap Step 3 and let go — you're now on track 3, one of Move's polyphonic sounds. (The screen briefly shows TRACK 3 and what it plays.)
  2. The pads now play pitched notes, snapped to the project's key and scale. Tap around to hear them. + / − shifts the octave.
  3. To sequence a note, hold a pad and tap a step button — that step gets the held note.
  4. For a chord, hold two or three pads and tap a step (up to eight notes per step).
  5. Press Play if it isn't already running. Track 3 plays alongside your drums.

A new project starts in a random key and scale. To change them, open Project Settings ([Shift] + [Step 2]), choose Key or Scale, click, turn to a new one and click. If your clips hold notes it asks whether to move them, and you hear the new key while it asks. See Key & Scale in the manual.

Lesson 3 — Shape the notes with sequencer effects

Every clip carries its own sequencer effects — they work on the notes, not the sound — reached through the parameter banks.

  1. Make sure you're on your melodic track (track 3) in Track View.
  2. Hold the jog for the bank map, and tap the DELAY pad — in the FX column (the fourth column of pads), third pad down. The screen's map shows which pad is which, and its header then reads DELAY.
  3. Turn knob 3 (REPTS) up to 3 — each note now echoes three times.
  4. Turn knob 5 (PITFB) to +5 — the echoes climb in pitch as they repeat.

These settings belong to this clip only. They're non-destructive: they transform playback without changing your written notes, so returning a knob to its default undoes it cleanly. Explore the other banks (NOTE FX, HARMONY, SEQ ARP) the same way — hold the jog, tap a pad, let go, turn the knobs. The Sequencer Effects chapter covers every one.

Lesson 4 — Launch clips and build a scene

So far you've been editing one clip per track. Each track holds 16 clips, and a row of clips across all tracks is a scene.

  1. Tap Note/Session to return to Session View. Columns are tracks 1–8; the top row of pads is row 1, where the clips you've made so far live.
  2. Hold Shift and tap the empty pad in track 3's column, row 2. Track 3 switches to that empty clip (and goes quiet), and it opens in Track View. Make a different melodic pattern, then tap Note/Session to come back.
  3. Tap track 3's row-1 clip to launch it again, then its row-2 clip — track 3 swaps patterns while the drums keep going. Launching one clip only replaces what was playing on that track.
  4. To switch a whole row at once, tap a side button (the buttons left of the grid, top one = row 1) or a step button (step 1 = row 1, step 2 = row 2…). Launch row 2: the drums stop, because their row-2 cell is empty. Launch row 1 and everything comes back.

Launching a single clip changes only its track. Launching a scene switches every track at once — an empty cell in that row silences its track. More in Arranging and Scenes.

Lesson 5 — A taste of Performance Mode

Performance Mode grabs a short loop of whatever's playing and lets you mangle it live with a grid of effects.

  1. In Session View, with your pattern playing, tap the Loop button. The pad grid turns into a mod grid and stays that way (tap [Loop] again to leave; or hold [Loop] to use it only while held).
  2. The bottom row's pads 1–5 are capture lengths, from 1/32 up to 1/2 bar. Hold one and the music loops that slice for as long as you hold it; let go and it plays on as written.
  3. The three rows above are mods: magenta = pitch tricks, yellow = volume/gate, blue = wild. Tap a pad to switch its mod on (tap again to switch it off), then hold a length pad — the mods work on the captured loop.
  4. The step buttons are presets — tap one of slots 1–8 to recall a ready-made combination (try slot 1, "Float"), hold a length pad to hear it, and tap the step again to turn it off.

Performance Mode is deep — capture lengths, latching, and 16 preset slots are all covered in Performance Mode.

Lesson 6 — Save your work

dAVEBOx saves as you go — whenever you stop the transport, a moment after your last edit while stopped, and whenever you leave. There is no save button to press.

  • Shift + Back saves and leaves dAVEBOx, handing the Move back to official Schwung. It asks first — turn the jog to Yes and click.
  • Project Settings → Quit does the same.
  • Project Settings → Suspend session parks dAVEBOx instead: it keeps playing in the background while you use Move.
  • A reboot returns you to official Schwung (unless dAVEBOx is your boot default).
  • The power button saves and turns the Move off (it asks first).

For named backups you can return to, use Save state in Project Settings — it keeps up to 16 timestamped snapshots per project. See Snapshots.

Where to go next

You now know enough to make complete patterns. When you're ready for more:

  • Choosing sounds — give tracks 5–8 a Schwung instrument, add audio effects, and set levels from each track's TRACK CONFIG menu: Choosing a track's sound.
  • Editing notes precisely — hold a step and the knobs act on that step's notes (length, velocity, nudge, probability, ratchets): Editing notes.
  • Longer clips and loops — clips can run up to 256 steps; hold Loop in Track View to set the loop window: Clip length & the loop.
  • Recording live — press Record to capture pad playing into a clip: Recording.
  • Automation — record knob moves that play back with the clip: Automation.
  • The Conductor — a track that transposes all the others in real time: The Conductor.
  • Exporting to Ableton Live — Project Settings → Export to Ableton renders the whole project to an .ablbundle: Export to Live.

And whenever you need a quick reminder of a control, the manual's Quick Reference lists every gesture on one screen.

Have fun.

3

The Basics

3.1The Controls

Each named button also works as a modifier when you hold it. The Quick Reference lists every gesture.

The four side buttons left of the pads launch the active track's clips in Track View, and whole scenes in Session View. [+] and [−] shift the pads' octave; on a drum track they shift the lane bank, and in Session View the rows.

3.2Transport

Press [Play] to start and stop. With modifiers:

  • To restart from the top, hold [Shift] and press [Play].
  • In Track View, hold [Loop] and press [Play] to restart with the current clip at the page you are looking at.
  • To turn the metronome on or off, hold [Mute] and press [Play].
  • To stop every clip while playing, hold [Delete] and press [Play]. While stopped, the same gesture sends a MIDI panic.

dAVEBOx can also lock to Move's transport or send clock to external gear; see Clock Follow.

3.3Switching Views

On either view's overview (its home screen), press [Note/Session] to switch between Track View and Session View. Hold it to peek at the other view.

Anywhere else, such as a bank page, a menu or a dialog, [Note/Session] closes everything and takes you to Session View in one press.

[Back] steps out one level at a time. Hold [Back] to go straight to the overview.

3.4Reading the Screen

The Track View overview shows, from top to bottom:

  • The header: the bank the knobs are on and, at the right, what the track plays. [MV1] is Move instrument 1, [CH3] MIDI channel 3, [TR2] track 2's instrument, [CNDT] the Conductor and [--] nothing loaded; otherwise a Schwung instrument's short name.
  • The key and scale, and the track's input velocity (VEL:LIVE means velocity follows how hard you play). On a drum track, the lane bank and the selected lane's note instead of the key.
  • The track numbers. A box marks the active track, a muted track's number blinks, and a soloed one is filled in.
  • The clip letters (A–P), filled while the clip plays or is about to.
  • The page bar: the page you are viewing is solid, the page playing is outlined, and a tick marks the playhead. A small mark at either end means there are notes outside the loop.
  • The footer: what the controls do here. HLD BANKS means hold the jog for the bank map, TCH EDIT means touch a knob or the jog to see the bank's page, and SHFT TRK means [Shift] picks the track.

In Session View the footer reads HLD BANKS TCH MIX: touch a knob or the jog for the mixer page.

3.5Selecting a Track

In either view, hold [Shift] and turn the jog to change the active track.

In Track View you can also hold the jog for the bank map and press [Step 1–8].

In Session View, tapping a clip pad selects its track and also launches or stops that clip. To open the clip in Track View instead, hold [Shift] and tap its pad.

3.6Menus, Lists and Typing

To open Project Settings, hold [Shift] and press [Step 2]. Every row is listed in Project Settings and Settings for the Whole Move; many also have a [Shift] + Step shortcut, listed in the Quick Reference.

In a list, turn the jog to move and press it to open or change a row. A number shows in [brackets] while you change it; press again to set it. In a list of choices, [Back] leaves the value as it was. In Project Settings, [Back] also cancels a change in progress.

3.6.1 Typing a Name

The on-screen keyboard opens whenever you name something. Turn the jog to a key and click to type it. The last page of keys holds symbols, the comma among them.

3.6.2 Speaking a Name

You can also speak a name: on the keyboard, hold [Record], speak, and let go. Dictation is an add-on that you install once from Project Settings (see Dictation).

  • The limit is 30 seconds per take, and it understands English only.
  • It works only while the music is stopped.
  • If you have not typed anything yet, what you say replaces the name; otherwise it is added after it. Commas and the closing full stop are left out.
  • It listens through the Move's microphone, or through the line input whenever a cable is plugged in, so anything else playing into the line input is heard too. Input monitoring is switched off while you talk.
  • It can't be used while the sampler ([Shift] + Volume + Sampling) is in use.

Press [Back] to cancel the dictation, and again to leave the keyboard. While a message card is up, the keys under it don't respond; press [Back] to take it down.

3.7Copy, Delete and Undo

These work the same way on steps, clips, drum lanes, pages and scenes:

  • To copy, hold [Copy], press the thing you want to copy, then press where it should go.
  • To cut instead, hold [Shift] as well as [Copy].
  • To clear something, hold [Delete] and press it.
  • To reset something, clearing it and returning its settings to their defaults, hold [Shift] and [Delete] and press it.

What each one keeps is described with the thing itself: steps, clips, drum lanes, pages, scenes, Audio and Slicer clips, banks and projects.

[Undo] reverses the last edit, and [Shift] + [Undo] redoes it. It is one step deep.

A few changes cannot be undone: a committed Key or Scale transpose, and a Trim or Normalize that overwrites a sample (see SAMPLE).

4

Banks and the Bank Map

VideoTutorial 1.3: The bank map (from 2:40)

In Track View the eight knobs play a bank: one page of related controls. To choose a bank, hold the jog for the bank map, tap a pad, and let go.

Each track remembers its bank. In Session View the knobs are the mixer, and holding the jog brings up the Session map instead. See The session mixer.

4.1The Bank Map

While you hold the jog, the left 4×4 pads become a map of the track's banks, and the screen shows the same map. You can tap as many pads as you like before you let go.

The four columns of pads are groups, and each group's banks run from top to bottom:

  • IN: what you play into the track. PAD MODE, LIVE ARP and RPT GROOVE.
  • CTRL: what moves the parameters. MACROS, AUTOMATION, and MIX at the foot.
  • SEQ: the sequence. STEP, CLIP, DRUM LANE, ALL LANES and INPUT.
  • FX: the sequencer effects, in the order the notes pass through them. NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY, SEQ ARP and REMIX. On a drum track they act on the selected lane.

A bank the track doesn't have leaves its pad dark, so a bank is always on the same pad. On a drum track, RPT GROOVE takes LIVE ARP's pad, DRUM LANE takes CLIP's, and ALL LANES sits below it. Audio and Slicer tracks put SAMPLE or SLICER on INST's pad and REMIX on DELAY's, and an Audio track has INPUT below CLIP.

On a Conductor the second column is the RSPD group, which sets how the other tracks respond. See The Conductor's banks.

4.1.1 Screens on the Map

Three pads open screens rather than banks: CONFIG opens TRACK CONFIG, AUTO the AUTOMATION screen, and INST the track's instrument. The screen opens when you let go of the jog, and it doesn't change the bank you are on.

4.1.2 More on the Map

In Track View, [Steps 1–8] on the map switch track. The map stays up, now showing the new track's banks.

In Track View, the right-hand pads open the track's module editors: MIDI FX above INSTRUMENT in the third column, and FX 1–4 down the far-right column. Each opens when you let go. A MIDI track has only MIDI FX, and a Conductor has none.

To switch view under the map, keep holding the jog and press [Note/Session].

To jump straight to LIVE ARP, hold [Shift] and hold [Step 11].

4.1.3 From Inside a Screen

Inside a menu, TRACK CONFIG, a module's editor (Move's own included) or the AUTOMATION screen, hold the jog for about a third of a second and the same map comes up over it. Tap a pad to leave the screen for that bank, or let go without tapping to stay. A quick press of the jog is still a press.

The map doesn't come up over the on-screen keyboard, over a question, or while [Shift], [Delete], [Copy], [Mute] or [Loop] is held.

4.2Playing a Bank

Touch a knob or the jog to see the bank's page; let go and the overview is back. Card Hold in Project Settings keeps the page up for half a second, one or two after you let go.

A knob with named choices, such as an arp style, opens its list while you turn it.

The knob LEDs light on every bank: knobs 1–4 white and 5–8 amber, with brightness following the value. A dark LED means nothing is on that knob.

On a bank with pages, turning the jog flips the pages. The paged banks are MIX (the levels, then the channel strip), an Audio clip's SAMPLE and a Slicer's SLICER editor.

LIVE ARP opened with [Shift] and a held [Step 11], the module editors, AUTOMATION and TRACK CONFIG stay up until you press [Back].

4.3Touch and Click

Some controls do more when you touch the knob and click the jog. These cells wear corner brackets, and while you touch one the bottom of the screen shows CLK and what the click will do.

A touch and click does one of these:

  • It switches a knob marked Alt in the bank tables to its alternate: Res to Zoom, Shift to Nudge, Dir to Reverse Style, Rand to Algo, and Rate to Clock Feedback. Touch and click again, press [Back], or leave the bank to switch it back.
  • It runs a one-shot action, such as Crop or Legato.
  • It opens an editor. Steps (knob 5) on SEQ ARP and LIVE ARP opens Arp Steps, any knob on RPT GROOVE switches between its Velocity and Nudge pages, and a knob on MACROS opens that macro.

On AUTOMATION, hold [Delete] and click the jog to clear the lane under the cursor.

4.4Resetting a Bank

To reset every parameter in the bank you are on, hold [Delete] and click the jog. One-shot actions (Stretch, Shift, Legato and Crop) are left alone, and on a paged bank only the page showing is reset. This doesn't work on ALL LANES, STEP, or the Conductor's ON/OFF, OCTAVE and TIMING banks. On a drum track's RPT GROOVE bank, or on any bank while Note Repeat is on, it resets the selected lane's groove.

On MACROS, the same gesture unassigns all eight macros on the track, after asking. Their values and automation are left alone.

To reset all the sequencer effects (NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY and SEQ ARP), hold [Shift] and [Delete] and click the jog. To reset the whole clip, notes and all parameters, hold [Shift] and [Delete] and press the clip's side button. Resets can be undone.

Resetting a parameter also clears its automation: a bank reset clears the automation for that bank's parameters, and clearing or resetting a clip clears all of it. On a drum track, clearing a single lane leaves automation alone, because a drum clip's automation covers the whole clip.

4.5Where Each Bank Is Covered

BankWhere it is covered
PAD MODEPad layouts (melodic), The SLICER editor (Slicer)
LIVE ARP, RPT GROOVELive input modifiers
MACROSThe MACROS bank
AUTOMATIONAutomation
MIXTrack levels and the channel strip
STEPEditing notes
CLIP, DRUM LANE, ALL LANESClip Timing and Grid; an Audio clip's CLIP in The banks
INPUTRecording into an Audio clip
SAMPLE, SLICERSAMPLE, The SLICER editor
NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY, SEQ ARPSequencer Effects
REMIXREMIX
ON/OFF, OCTAVE, TIMINGThe Conductor's banks
5

Projects

dAVEBOx keeps its own projects, separate from your Move Sets, which it never sees or changes.

5.1The Project Picker

VideoTutorial 7.1: Projects and Save state

To open the project picker, hold [Shift] and press [Step 1] from anywhere. The pads become your projects, 32 slots, each in its own color; the open project is solid white. A dim red pad is a project that can't open, but you can still rename, recolor or delete it.

5.1.1 Opening a Project

Tap a project to select it, then choose Load. Load stops playback first. To load a project at once, hold [Shift] and tap its pad.

5.1.2 Creating a Project

Tap an empty pad and confirm. The new project gets a random two-word name, such as Quiet Harbor. To create a project and open it in one press, hold [Shift] and tap the empty pad.

Once you have saved a template, creating a project asks Empty or Template.

5.1.3 Renaming and Coloring

Rename and Color are on the selected project's screen. Two projects can't share a name.

5.1.4 Copying and Deleting

To copy a project, hold [Copy], tap the project, then tap an empty pad.

To delete a project, hold [Delete], tap the project, then tap it again to confirm. If you delete the project you are in, dAVEBOx restarts at the project picker with nothing loaded.

5.1.5 When a Project Won't Open

If PROJECT DID NOT OPEN appears, choose Retry to try again, or press [Back] to return to the picker.

5.2Saving, Suspending and Leaving

VideoTutorial 7.1: Projects and Save state

dAVEBOx saves as you go, but never during playback: it saves when you stop the transport, a moment after your last edit while stopped, at the end of a recording, and when you suspend, quit or switch projects. There is no manual save; for named backups, use Save state.

A project has a size limit of about 1 MB. Past it, dAVEBOx shows PROJECT TOO BIG and saves only when you quit or suspend, until you remove some clips.

5.2.1 Leaving and Suspending

To leave dAVEBOx and hand the device back to official Schwung, hold [Shift] and press [Back] from anywhere, or choose Quit in Project Settings. Either one saves first.

To use Move while dAVEBOx keeps playing in the background, choose Suspend session in Project Settings. To come back, hold [Shift] and hold [Step 13] for half a second, or press [Shift] + [Step 13] twice quickly, or pick dAVEBOx SA in the Tools menu.

If dAVEBOx is your boot default, a reboot returns to dAVEBOx. To go back, hold [Back] at power-on and pick Schwung.

5.2.2 Powering Off

Tap or hold the power button and confirm. dAVEBOx saves before the Move turns off.

5.3Save States

For named backups, choose Save state in Project Settings, which keeps up to 16 dated snapshots per project; when all 16 are used it asks which one to replace. To restore one, choose Load state. Snapshots survive Clear Sess.

Snapshots saved by a different dAVEBOx version can't be loaded.

The other kinds of preset and snapshot are compared in Presets and Snapshots at a Glance.

5.4Templates

A template is a starting point for new projects. To save one, choose Save as Template... in Project Settings. It keeps each track's instrument, effects, MACROS and track settings, and the project settings. No clips, notes or automation come along, and every sequencer bank starts at its default. A Slicer comes along whole, sample included; Audio tracks arrive empty.

To use a template, see Creating a Project. To rename, replace or delete one, choose Templates... in Project Settings.

If a template uses a module this Move doesn't have, that slot starts empty (MODULES MISSING).

5.5Backing Up and Moving Projects

The Projects page of the web manager (move.local:7700, during a session) can download one project or all of them, templates included, as a file. Stop playback before you download the open project, or its last second of edits may not be in the file. See dAVEBOx and official Schwung.

To restore, upload a downloaded file, on this Move or another one. Each project is added on the first free pad; nothing on the Move is replaced, so restoring a project you still have gives you a second one named "Name (imported)".

Samples and recordings from your Move library aren't part of a project and don't travel with it.

5.6Compatibility and What's Saved

dAVEBOx opens every project an earlier version saved. A project saved by a newer dAVEBOx says PROJECT TOO NEW and is left as it is, never erased. Once saved, a project made before dAVEBOx 1.1 opens in dAVEBOx 1.0.0 without its automation.

dAVEBOx 1.1.3 and earlier can't read a project saved by this version, and ask to erase it. If you go back to one of those versions, answer No.

If you used dAVEBOx when it worked in your Move Sets, that work stays in those Sets. dAVEBOx projects start fresh.

6

Tempo, Key and Groove

Tempo, metronome, key, scale and groove belong to the project. You set them in Project Settings: hold [Shift] and press [Step 2]. Every row is listed in Project Settings.

6.1Tempo and Metronome

VideoTutorial 1.4: Tempo and key (from 3:47)

BPM sets the tempo, from 40 to 250. While Clock Follow is on, it reads Move and the project follows Move's tempo.

To tap the tempo, hold [Shift] and press [Step 5], then tap any pad in time.

Metro sets when the metronome sounds: Off, Cnt-In (the default, count-in only), Play or Always. Metro Vol sets its level, from 0 to 150 %.

To switch Metro between Cnt-In and Always, hold [Shift] and press [Step 6]. To turn the metronome on and off from the transport, hold [Mute] and press [Play].

6.2Key and Scale

Key sets the project's root note. Scale sets the scale that melodic tracks snap to. A new project starts in a random key and scale. To jump straight to Scale, hold [Shift] and press [Step 9].

Scale Aware sets whether scale-aware parameters move by scale degree (On, the default) or by semitone (Off).

Instruments and MIDI effects with a Host key setting follow dAVEBOx's key, scale and tempo live.

6.2.1 Moving Your Clips to a New Key

When you change Key or Scale and a melodic clip holds notes, TRANSPOSE CLIPS? asks whether to move the notes to the new key. While it asks, the pads show the new key and, if the music is playing, you hear the clips in it.

Key moves notes by the shortest distance. A new scale remaps notes by scale degree between scales of the same size, and otherwise to the nearest in-scale note. Drum tracks are untouched.

Note that a committed transpose can't be undone, so check the preview before you confirm.

6.3The Groove

VideoTutorial 6.4: Groove and swing (from 7:23)

One groove plays for the whole project. To jump to Groove Amt, hold [Shift] and press [Step 7].

SettingWhat it doesValuesDefault
GrooveThe project's timing feelOff, Browse..., Swing 1/16, Swing 1/8, the loaded grooveSwing 1/16
Groove AmtHow much of the groove is applied. On a swing: 50 % is straight, 66 % is triplet swing0–100 % (50–75 % on a swing)0 % (50 % on a swing)
Grv TimingHow much of the loaded groove's timing shifts are applied0–100 %The groove's own
Grv VelocityHow far notes are pulled toward the groove's velocities0–100 %The groove's own
Grv RandomHow much each note wanders from its place, differently every time0–100 %The groove's own

Grv Timing, Grv Velocity and Grv Random are shown only for a loaded groove. Off plays straight, whatever Groove Amt says.

6.3.1 Loading a Groove

Browse... opens a list of MIDI files and Ableton groove files (.agr). Turning the jog to a file plays it at once, over whatever is playing. Click the jog to keep it; [Back] restores the groove you had.

A MIDI file is read over its whole length, on the grid its notes were played on (1/16, swung 1/8 or triplets), up to 128 positions. If a file has several parts, dAVEBOx asks which one to use.

Notes the sequencer plays are moved both earlier and later. Arps, repeats, delay echoes and the looper are only ever moved later.

The loaded groove appears at the foot of the Groove list, so you can go to a swing and come back. It is saved inside the project, so it survives the file being removed.

6.3.2 Groove on Each Track

In a track's settings, Grv Amt reads Global. Turn it and that track takes its own amount instead, from 0 to 100 % in 5 % steps. With a loaded groove, Grv Timing, Grv Velocity and Grv Random work the same way on each track. Turn a row back down to Global and the track follows the project again.

6.3.3 Recording Under a Groove

With Input Quantize off, what you play is stored so that the groove plays it back at the moment you played it; it is not grooved a second time. With Input Quantize on, the note snaps to the grid and the groove moves it from there.

7

Tracks and Clips

dAVEBOx has 8 tracks. Each track holds 16 clips and plays one clip at a time. A track plays one instrument (see Choosing an instrument), except an Audio or Slicer track, which plays samples.

Track View always shows the current clip of the active track. To choose the bank that shapes the clip, hold the jog for the bank map and tap a pad. What goes into a clip is covered in Melodic Clips and Drum Clips.

7.1Track Type

TypeWhere you set itHow it works
MelodicMode, MelodicScale-snapped notes on the pads and steps. See Melodic Clips.
DrumMode, Drums32 drum lanes, each its own step sequence. See Drum Clips.
AudioInstmt/Dest, AudioA sample per clip. See Audio Tracks.
SlicerInstmt/Dest, SlicerOne sample, chopped; each clip is a sequence of slices. See Slicer Tracks.
ConductorInstmt/Dest, ConductorPlays no notes and transposes the other tracks. See The Conductor.

Mode is a row of the track's TRACK CONFIG menu. Audio, Slicer and Conductor are in the Instmt/Dest picker, after the Move instruments: hold [Shift] and click the jog on the Instmt/Dest row. Choosing an instrument in the same picker turns the track back into an ordinary one.

Track 1 of a new project starts as a drum track, and the rest as melodic. A track keeps its color, clips and routing whatever its type, so a Conductor's instrument is still there when you switch back.

7.2Changing Type

A track cannot change type while the transport is playing.

Changing type keeps your notes across all 16 clips. It resets the sequencer effects (NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY and SEQ ARP).

From melodic to drum, each pitch becomes its own lane and per-step conditions are dropped. Note that a clip with more than 32 pitches loses the least-used ones.

From drum to melodic, dAVEBOx does not ask. The lanes merge into one clip, with the length of the first lane that has notes, and per-step conditions are dropped.

Making a track the Conductor keeps the notes and their conditions, and clears effects, arps and automation. Only one track can be the Conductor. Choosing an instrument turns a Conductor back into a melodic track, without asking.

Choosing Audio or Slicer clears the track's notes. The track's instrument goes and its effects stay. The track plays through its own Schwung slot; a track that used a Move instrument takes one.

If you choose Audio on a track that plays an instrument and has clips, Resample the clips? asks first. Yes records each clip with notes into an Audio clip, so the track sounds the same, as in Flattening a track. No converts without recording, and the notes are cleared.

Leaving Audio or Slicer clears every clip's steps and lets go of the samples. One [Undo] brings it all back. The files stay in the project until you purge them.

7.3Switching Clips

The four side buttons launch the active track's clips. They follow the four clip rows shown in Session View, and the lit button is the clip you are editing.

To stop the playing clip at the end of its page, press its side button; press it again to cancel. To scroll the four visible clips by one, hold [Shift] and press the top or bottom side button.

The side buttons take the gestures in Copy, Delete and Undo:

  • [Copy] and a side button, then another side button, copies the clip to that slot. [Shift] and [Copy] cuts it.
  • [Delete] and a side button clears the clip's notes and automation, and frees its length for the next recording.
  • [Shift], [Delete] and a side button resets the clip: notes and all parameters.

7.4Clip Length and the Loop

VideoTutorial 3.9: Loop length and pages (from 10:10)

A clip plays its loop: up to 256 steps, shown as pages of 16. On a drum track, each lane has its own loop, set the same way (see Per-lane loops). [Left] and [Right] move between pages.

To grow or shrink the loop by one step, hold [Loop] and turn the jog. To double the loop and copy what is in it into the new half, hold [Shift] and press [Step 15].

Note that the loop length cannot be changed while a take is recording.

7.4.1 Seq Follow

Seq Follow keeps the step buttons on the page that is playing. It is one switch for the whole device and is remembered between sessions.

To turn it on or off, hold [Left] or [Right] and press [Play]; the transport is not affected. It works in the module editors too, but not in Session View. A small play-to-bar mark to the left of Vel: shows it is on.

If you press [Left] or [Right] while the transport runs, Seq Follow pauses and the mark blinks. It follows again the next time the transport stops. Restarting with [Shift] and [Play], or [Loop] and [Play], is not a stop, so the pause stays.

7.4.2 The Loop View

Hold [Loop] for the loop view. The step buttons now stand for pages, and a page inside the loop lights in the track color. While you hold [Loop]:

  • Turn the jog to grow or shrink the loop from its end.
  • Press a step button to end the loop on that page. The loop runs from page 1, or from the loop's start if it starts later.
  • Hold one step button and press another to set the loop to the range between them.

Notes outside the loop are kept, and return when you widen it.

To keep the loop view up hands-free, tap [Loop] instead of holding it; [Loop] blinks white and the pads keep playing. Press [Loop] or [Back] to close it.

Note that a press of [Loop] that already does something else still does only that. On a drum track with a latched repeat it releases the repeat, and while the arpeggiator's latch holds notes it clears them.

7.4.3 Copying Pages

To copy one page of a clip onto another, hold [Loop] and [Copy], press a lit page, then press another page. Keep holding [Copy] to paste onto more pages. [Shift] and [Copy] cuts instead. One [Undo] takes a paste back.

A paste past the end of the clip makes the clip longer, and a paste before the loop's start moves the start back. Steps outside the loop count as empty. Automation stays where it is.

On a drum track, page copying copies the selected lane, or every lane on the ALL LANES bank.

7.4.4 Cropping the Loop

The clip transforms (Stretch, Shift, Nudge, Legato and Zoom) do nothing unless the loop starts on [Step 1].

Crop makes the loop the whole clip: on the CLIP bank, touch knob 6 and click the jog. Everything outside the loop is removed. One [Undo] brings it back.

8

Melodic Clips

The Sequencer Effects and Automation that shape a clip have their own chapters, and recording into a clip is in Recording and Capture.

8.1Playing and Placing Notes

VideoTutorial 3.1: Placing notes

The pads play notes from the current key and scale. [+] and [−] shift them by an octave.

While you hold notes, on the pads or an external keyboard, the screen names the note or chord in brackets, such as [F#3]. Middle C is C3, as on Move. A raised dot after a chord name, as in [A♭MAJ7˙], means the chord is played without its third.

8.1.1 Placing Notes on the Steps

To place a note, play it on a pad, then press an empty step button. The step gets the last note you played, at velocity 100, or at the track's fixed VelIn if it has one. To clear a step, press it again. These step gestures work on drum steps too (see Drum Clips).

To edit a step, hold it: the knobs on screen now act on that step (see Editing notes). An empty step stays empty until you tap a pad while holding it. To stretch a note, hold its step and press a later step (also in Editing notes).

If you press several steps at once, each empty step gets the last note. On a melodic track, a filled step after the first is silenced but keeps its notes; do it again to bring them back. On a drum track, a filled step is cleared.

To copy a step's notes within the clip, hold [Copy], press the step, then press another step. [Shift] and [Copy] cuts. To clear a step and any automation on it, hold [Delete] and press the step.

8.2Pad Layouts

Each melodic track has its own pad layout. There are five:

  • Scale (the default) shows only in-scale notes. Each row starts three scale notes above the row below.
  • Chrom shows all 12 semitones, with in-scale notes highlighted. Each row carries on from the end of the row below.
  • Piano shows two keyboard octaves, and can switch to a bass neck. See Piano and Bass.
  • Chord plays a whole chord from one pad. See The Chord layout.
  • Custom puts chords you build yourself on the bottom row, and the Scale layout on the other three. See The Custom layout.

To choose a layout, open the Pad Mode bank (the top pad of the IN column on the bank map) and turn knob 1, Mode. Each layout keeps its settings when you switch away and back. You can also hold [Shift] and press [Step 8] to step through the layouts.

To reset the current layout's settings, hold [Delete] and click the jog on the Pad Mode bank. Mode, Piano's Instr and your Custom chords stay. [Undo] brings the settings back.

Note that a Conductor's pads have Scale and Chrom only, chosen with [Shift] and [Step 8]. A Conductor has no Pad Mode bank.

8.2.1 Piano and Bass

The Piano layout shows two keyboard octaves from C: the lower on the bottom two rows, the higher on the top two. In each, the bottom row is the white keys and the row above is the black keys.

Oct A and Trans A move the bottom octave (zone A), and Oct B and Trans B the top one (zone B).

The Instr knob switches the pads to Bass: four strings, E A D G from the bottom row up, with the open string and seven frets across each. Bass has one Oct and one Trans for the whole neck.

8.2.2 Splitting the Pads

The Scale and Chrom layouts can split the pads into two zones on the Pad Mode bank:

  • Split is None, Vert or Horz. Vert splits left from right; Horz splits the bottom two rows from the top two. Zone A is the left or bottom one.
  • Oct A and Oct B set each zone's octave.
  • Trans A and Trans B set where each zone starts. In Scale they count scale notes (+2 in C major starts on E). In Chrom they count semitones.

Zone B shows its colors the other way round, so the two zones read apart. Scale and Chrom share the split and the octaves; each keeps its own Transpose.

8.2.3 The Octave Buttons

To move only zone B, hold [Shift] and press [+] or [−]. Zone B is the B split, Piano's top octave, or the pads above the chords in the Chord and Custom layouts.

8.3The Chord Layout

VideoTutorial 3.8: The Chord layout (from 8:52)

The Chord layout plays a whole chord from one pad, always in the track's key and scale.

  • The bottom row holds eight chords: by default I ii iii IV V vi vii° and I an octave up. They are colored by function and follow key and scale changes.
  • Row 2 holds modifiers: 7, 9, sus2, sus4, add9 and 5. Hold one while you tap a chord, or tap one while a chord is held to change it as it sounds.
  • The last two pads of row 2, Inv− and Inv+, move the voicing down or up one note. Hold one before a chord for that tap, or tap it while a chord is held; each tap moves it further.
  • Row 3 holds the notes of the last chord you played, to strum or pick. They stay after you let go.
  • The top row is the scale, with the key's root on the fourth pad.

To write a whole chord into a step, hold the step and tap the chord.

8.3.1 The Chord Layout's Settings

KnobSettingWhat it does
MapDiatonic, FunctionHow the chords sit on the bottom row. Function groups them by job: home (I vi iii), away (IV ii), pulling home (V vii°), then I an octave up.
VoicingMoves every chord at once.
SmoothOff, Follow, AnchorFollow gives each chord the voicing nearest the last one. Anchor uses the voicing nearest one chord you choose on the Anchor knob.
BassOff, −1, −2Adds the root one or two octaves below.
Pad OctMoves rows 3 and 4 by octaves, as [Shift] and [+] or [−] does.
SlotsPlay, SelectIn Select, the chord pads are silent and only choose what row 3 strums.

8.3.2 Editing a Chord

To edit a chord, hold its pad while on the Pad Mode bank. The page switches to that chord until you let go. Its knobs are Root, Stack, Inversion, Spread, Bass (Off, Root, 3rd or 5th) and Octave. To reset the chord, touch knob 8, Reset, and click the jog.

On every other bank, a held chord leaves the knobs alone, so you can play chords and turn other knobs at the same time.

Note that a stack with no in-key version on that chord, such as sus4 on IV in a major key, plays the plain chord.

8.4The Custom Layout

The Custom layout gives you eight chords of your own on the bottom row, with the Scale layout on the other three rows. A chord keeps its exact notes when the key or scale changes. Chords are saved per track.

To play a chord, tap its pad; an empty chord pad is dark and silent. To write a whole chord into a step, hold the step and tap the chord.

8.4.1 Building a Chord

To build or edit a chord, hold its pad and tap pads on the upper rows. Each tap adds that note, or removes it if the chord already has it. A chord holds up to six notes. Notes added this way are not written into a recording in progress.

You can also work notes first: hold the notes on the upper rows and tap an empty chord pad, and it takes them (the lowest six). A pad that already has a chord just plays.

Both ways work from a USB keyboard on dAVEBOx's MIDI-in channel. Keys used this way are not recorded or captured.

8.4.2 Copying, Moving and Clearing Chords

  • To copy a chord, hold [Copy], tap the chord, then tap each pad that should get it. [Shift] and [Copy] moves it instead.
  • To move one chord an octave, hold its pad and press [+] or [−]. This works only when Hold is set to Assign.
  • To clear a chord, hold [Delete] and tap its pad.

[Shift] and [+] or [−] moves only the upper rows; use it to reach notes in another octave while building a chord.

8.4.3 The Custom Layout's Settings

KnobWhat it does
HoldAssign (the default): holding a chord pad edits it. Play: holding a chord pad just plays it, and holding notes never fills an empty pad.
Chd OctThe chord row's octave.
Pad OctThe upper rows' octave.
TransWhere the upper rows start, counted in scale notes.

To build a chord by name, hold a chord pad while on the Pad Mode bank. The page becomes its card, with the same knobs as the Chord layout's card:

  • Root: any note.
  • Stack: Maj, Min, Dim, Aug, Sus2, Sus4, 7, Maj7, Min7, m7b5, Dim7, 6, Min6, Add9, 9, Maj9, Min9, 7sus4 or 5.
  • Inv: the inversion.
  • Sprd: Open lifts the second-lowest note an octave.
  • Bass: Off, Root, 3rd or 5th.
  • Oct: the octave.
  • Reset: touch knob 8 and click the jog, and the pad empties.

A turn replaces the pad's notes with the chord on the card. One [Undo] brings back what the pad held before. The card works with Hold set to Assign or Play.

8.5Several Notes on One Step

A step holds up to eight notes. Hold one or more pads, then press a step; or hold a step, then tap pads one at a time. Tap a held note again to remove it.

8.6Editing Notes

VideoTutorial 3.2: Editing a step (from 1:02)

Holding a step points whatever knobs are on screen at that step.

On the STEP bank (the top pad of the SEQ column on the bank map), the knobs are the note's own settings, listed below.

On a module editor, MACROS, or a sequencer-effect bank (NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY, SEQ ARP, and CLIP's Dir), the knobs write a lock at that step (see Automation). LIVE ARP and the rest of CLIP do nothing under a held step.

KnobAdjusts
1 · NotePitch, by scale degree
2 · OctPitch, by octave
3 · LengNote length (gate)
4 · VelVelocity
5 · NudgTiming, up to ±1 step
6 · IterIteration (see Per-step conditions)
7 · ProbProbability
8 · RatchRatchet

Edits apply to every note in the step. A note nudged past half a step moves to the neighbouring step when you let go.

8.6.1 Reaching the Note Settings From Any Bank

To open a step's STEP page from any bank, hold a step with notes and turn the jog right; turn it left, or let go, to return.

8.6.2 Stretching a Note or a Lock

To stretch a note, hold its step until the Edit step card shows, then press a later step. Press that step again to shorten the note by one step. [Left] and [Right] still page, so a note can stretch past the current page.

Note that pressing steps together, without the pause, toggles them instead.

If the last thing you did while holding the step was turn a knob to set a lock, pressing a later step stretches that lock's value up to it instead, as on the AUTOMATION screen. The range lights orange while you hold. Editing the note again, with a STEP knob or a pad, puts the press back to stretching the note.

8.6.3 Per-Step Conditions

VideoTutorial 3.4: Steps that decide for themselves (from 4:21)

  • Iteration (Iter) plays the step only on certain passes of the loop: 2:3 plays on the 2nd pass of every three. The counter resets when you stop the transport and press [Play] again.
  • Probability (Prob) gives the step a chance of playing, from 100 % down to 1 %. The roll is per note, so chords thin out unevenly.
  • Ratchet (Ratch) retriggers the step 2, 3 or 4 times within its slot.

Removing the step's last note clears its conditions.

9

Drum Clips

On a drum track, each sound is a lane: its own step sequence, with its own length, timing and effects. A track has 32 lanes, each mapped to a MIDI note.

9.1The Drum Pads

The left 4x4 holds 16 drum lanes: tap one to hear and select it, and the step buttons show that lane. The right 4x4 holds velocity zones, or a Note Repeat mode. [+] and [−] switch between lane bank A and bank B.

On the DRUM LANE bank, the selected lane is the track's color and lanes with hits are light grey. On every other bank, the selected lane is white and lanes with hits are the track's color. A muted lane is always off.

9.2Placing Hits

VideoTutorial 2.1: Lanes, hits and velocity

To place hits, select a lane, then press the step buttons to add or clear its hits.

The 16 velocity zones, from 8 at the bottom left to 127 at the top right, set the velocity of the hits you place next and play the selected lane at that velocity. With a step held, a zone pad sets that hit's velocity, or places the hit if the step was empty.

A lane's sound is set by its MIDI note, on the NOTE FX bank: knob 1 moves it by an octave and knob 2 by a semitone. A new drum track's bank A plays notes 36–51, so a Move kit lines up pad for pad.

Editing a hit works the same as editing a note, without the pitch knobs: Leng, Vel and Nudg are on knobs 1–3, and Iter, Prob and Ratch on 5–7. Note that on a drum hit, pressing the same later step again does not shorten it.

9.3Per-Lane Loops

VideoTutorial 2.2: Euclidean rhythms and per-lane loops (from 1:39)

Each lane has its own loop length, so lanes of different lengths make a polyrhythm from one clip.

To set the selected lane's length, hold [Loop] and turn the jog, or use the loop view. On the ALL LANES bank, these set every lane at once.

The transforms need a lane's loop to start on [Step 1]. To crop, touch knob 6 on DRUM LANE for the selected lane, or knob 5 on ALL LANES for every lane, and click the jog.

9.4Note Repeat

VideoTutorial 2.3: Note Repeat (from 3:08)

Note Repeat retriggers a lane at a steady rate. Hold [Shift] and press [Step 8] to cycle the right pads between velocity zones and the two repeat modes. Opening a project puts the right pads back on velocity zones.

The bottom two rows of the right pads are rates, straight and then triplet. The top two rows are an 8-step gate mask (see the drum pad diagram).

In Rpt1, the selected lane repeats while you hold a rate pad. Velocity follows pad pressure, and you can change lanes while holding.

In Rpt2, tap a rate pad to assign it to the selected lane, then hold a lane pad. Hold several lane pads for layered repeats.

9.4.1 Latching a Repeat

To latch, hold [Loop] and tap a rate pad in Rpt1, or a lane pad in Rpt2; you can also press [Loop] while already holding one. Latched lanes light cyan.

To release a latched pad, tap it again. To release every latch on the track, press [Loop] with no pads held, or hold [Delete] and press [Loop]. Stopping the transport clears them too.

9.4.2 The Gate Mask

The gate mask is a looping on and off pattern over the repeats. Tap a gate pad to toggle it.

To set the mask's cycle length, from 1 to 8, hold [Loop] and tap a gate pad. This also turns every gate in the cycle back on. To reset a step's groove, hold [Delete] and tap its gate pad.

Per-step velocity and timing are on the RPT GROOVE bank.

9.5Copying, Clearing and Muting Lanes

The lane pads take the gestures in Copy, Delete and Undo, and a mute and solo of their own:

  • To copy a lane, hold [Copy], tap its pad, then tap another lane. The destination keeps its own MIDI note. [Shift] and [Copy] cuts.
  • To clear a lane's hits, hold [Delete] and tap its pad.
  • To reset a lane, hold [Shift] and [Delete] and tap its pad. This resets its hits, length, loop, effects and repeat groove, but keeps its sound.
  • To mute a lane, hold [Mute] and tap its pad. To solo it, hold [Shift] and [Mute] and tap its pad.
  • To clear the track's lane mutes and solos, hold [Delete] and press [Mute].
10

Recording and Capture

To record knob moves as automation, see Making it. To record audio into an Audio clip, see Recording into an Audio clip.

10.1Recording

VideoTutorial 3.5: Recording (from 5:40)

Press [Record] to record into the active clip. If the transport is stopped, a 1-bar count-in plays first. While the transport plays, [Record] punches in and out at the moment you press.

A take that began with the count-in into an empty clip grows a page at a time for as long as you play. Press [Record] to finish; the clip keeps the page the playhead is in, so press it in the last page you want.

Recording adds to what is there and never erases. For a clean take, hold [Delete] and press the clip's side button first; that also frees its length, so the take sizes itself.

Notes played in the last half-beat of the count-in land on [Step 1]. Recording follows the active track if you switch tracks during a take.

Note that recording needs the Forward playback direction. Otherwise the screen shows REC UNAVAILABLE: set Dir to Fwd, or choose Bake Now (see Bake).

10.2Step Recording

VideoTutorial 3.7: Step recording (from 8:03)

Step recording places notes one step at a time, without the transport running. It works on melodic tracks only.

To start, stop the transport and hold [Shift] and press [Record]. A blinking white cursor starts at the first step of the page you are viewing. Tap a pad, or several for a chord; the cursor moves on when you let go.

To tie a note longer, press [Right] while holding its pads; [Left] with the pads held takes one step back off.

To enter a rest, press [Right] alone. [Left] alone steps back and erases what you entered there in this session; notes already in the clip stay. The cursor stops at the clip's last step and never wraps.

To leave, press [Record] or [Back]. You can also press [Play] to hear the result. One [Undo] takes back the whole step recording session.

Note that Live Merge is unavailable while step recording is open.

10.3Capture

VideoTutorial 3.6: Capture (from 6:33)

dAVEBOx is always listening: notes you play while not recording are held in a buffer, and [Capture] writes them into the clip. [Capture] blinks white while there is something to keep. It works on melodic and drum clips.

The buffer includes external MIDI and your knob moves, which land as automation. With LIVE ARP on, what is kept is the arpeggio you heard, not the pads you held. With a MIDI effect set to Pre, what is kept is what the effect played (see Editing a module).

One [Undo] takes back any capture. To clear the buffer, knob moves included, hold [Shift] and press [Capture].

10.3.1 What Capture Does

Transport and clipWhat [Capture] does
PlayingAdds the buffered notes where you played them. Into an empty clip, the take keeps its beat and starts on the next bar.
Stopped, empty projectReads a tempo from your playing and offers it with nearby candidates, sizes a clip to whole bars, and starts it.
Stopped, current clip emptyFits the take to the current tempo; turn the jog to pick how many bars, or hold [Shift] and turn to fine-stretch.
Stopped, current clip holds notesOpens Session View: tap a blinking empty clip on that track to keep the take, or press [Record] to cancel.

10.3.2 What the Buffer Holds

The buffer holds at most the last 8 bars. Playing over a spot you already played on an earlier lap replaces that lap.

The buffer starts afresh when you select another track, edit a clip by hand, launch a clip or scene, arm [Record], start or stop the transport, or pause for about two bars. Every press of [Capture] empties it, even one that found nothing to keep.

10.3.3 Capturing Encoder Moves

Knob moves are buffered only while the transport runs with [Record] off. One press of [Capture] commits them into the clip you heard them in, as editable lanes. Another lap replaces what the last lap kept, and stopping the transport clears them.

11

Importing MIDI

VideoTutorial 7.2: MIDI import and export (from 1:01)

You can fill a clip with the notes from a standard MIDI file (.mid, .midi, .smf, .kar or .rmi), on any track except a Conductor.

To open the MIDI browser, go to the CLIP or DRUM LANE bank, touch knob 8 and click the jog.

Keep your MIDI files anywhere in your user data folder; the Files page of the web manager uploads there. No MIDI files come with dAVEBOx.

11.1The List

Every file plays as you land on it, in place of what the track plays, in time with the song if the track is playing. DRM marks an all-drums file. A file with several parts shows NAME> and its part count; click it to see the parts.

Click the jog on a file or part to open its card. To leave the browser from anywhere, hold [Back].

Each track remembers its own last file while you work.

11.2The Card

The card is the file you picked, still playing. Each new file starts at Start 1, Res 1/16, Stretch x1 and its own length.

KnobParameterWhat it does
1 · StartStartThe bar of the file to start from
2 · BarsBarsHow many bars land in the clip, up to what the file has from Start and the clip holds at this resolution (1/16 holds 16 bars of 4/4)
3 · ResResolutionThe clip's step size, 1/32 to a whole bar. Notes keep their timing
4 · StretchStretch/8, /4, /2, x1, x2, x4 or x8 of its length
5 · OctOctaveUp to three octaves up or down
6 · SemiSemitoneUp to eleven semitones up or down
7 · ScaleScaleOn folds every note into the project's key and scale (between two scale notes, it goes up); Off plays it as written
8TempoThe file's tempo in BPM, if it has one

Oct and Semi move the notes before Scale folds them.

On a drum track, knob 5 is Map instead: GM (lanes play their General MIDI notes), Move (Move's kit layout) or Off (starting from the lane you are on). The right-hand pads are the file's sounds. Hold one to hear it alone and see where every sound goes, and tap a lane pad to put it there; tap the lane pad again to take it off. Up to eight sounds are placed.

The line under the top knobs shows the file's notes, with brackets around what will land. The top right says what won't land: CUT (outside the brackets), OVER (past the clip's note limit) or OFF (drum sounds with no lane). REPLACES means the clip already has notes.

To mute or unmute the preview, hold [Shift] and click the jog.

11.3Loading

To load the file, click the jog on the card and confirm. The notes replace the clip you are on. On a drum track only the lanes a sound goes to are replaced. One [Undo] takes the whole load back.

Only notes come in: no controllers, pitch bend or program changes, and not the file's tempo. Bars follow the file's time signature.

A melodic clip's automation is cleared with the load ([Undo] brings it back). A melodic clip holds up to 512 notes, and so does a drum lane.

The step buttons are blocked while you browse.

12

Clip Timing and Grid

Some parameters rewrite your notes permanently. They are marked Yes in the Rewrites notes column, and [Undo] reverses them. The rest only change how the clip plays. To reset a bank, see Banks and the Bank Map.

The CLIP bank holds different things on each track type:

TrackWhat CLIP holdsWhere it is covered
MelodicGrid, stretch, shift, legato, input quantize, crop, direction, MIDI importThe CLIP Bank
DrumDRUM LANE and ALL LANES take its placeThe DRUM LANE Bank
AudioMode, Strch and Dir; the sample itself is on SAMPLEAudio track banks
SlicerAs a melodic clip's, plus >Seq› to lay the slices out as stepsSlicer track banks
ConductorTiming and direction, plus Cond LockThe Conductor's banks

12.1The CLIP Bank

VideoTutorial 3.3: The CLIP bank (from 2:36)

KnobWhat it doesRewrites notesDefault
1 · RESResolution: keeps the pattern's steps and changes how long a step is. Alternate (ZOOM): keeps the timing and changes how many steps it takes.Yes1/16
2 · STRCHStretch: turn right to double the clip, left to halve it.Yes—
3 · SHIFTShift: rotates the notes in the loop by whole steps. Alternate (NUDGE): finer.Yes0
4 · LGTOLegato: lengthens every note in the loop to reach the next.Yes—
5 · INQNTInput Quantize: snaps recorded notes to the grid (Off, 1/64 … 1/4t).NoOff
6 · CROPCrop: the loop becomes the whole clip.Yes—
7 · DIRDirection: Forward, Backward or ping-pong. Alternate (REVRS): Reverse Style.NoFwd
8 · IMPRTImport MIDI: fills the clip from a MIDI file.Yes—

To switch a knob marked Alternate to its alternate parameter, touch the knob and click the jog. Press [Back] to switch it back.

Stretch makes one change per touch; let go and touch again to stretch again. It is refused with COMPRESS LIMIT when notes would collide, and doubling is refused past step 256, or with NOTES PAST THE LOOP END / CROP FIRST if notes lie past the loop's end.

A note shifted off the loop's end comes round to its start.

Legato, Crop and Import MIDI are actions: touch the knob and click the jog. Legato lengthens the last note to the loop's end. Crop moves the loop to step 1 and removes everything outside it, automation included, as one [Undo]. Import MIDI is covered in Importing MIDI.

Zoom, Stretch, Shift and Legato need the loop to start at step 1. If it starts later, Stretch says LOOP STARTS AFTER STEP 1 / CROP FIRST. Crop puts the loop at step 1.

Input Quantize is one value per track, shared with the ALL LANES bank.

12.1.1 Direction and Reverse Style

The two ping-pong directions differ only in which end they start from.

Reverse Style, the alternate of DIR, sets what backward playback does to each note:

  • Step (the default) reverses the order of the steps. Each note still triggers at its start and sounds unchanged.
  • Audio also mirrors each note within its slot, with the note-on at the note's end and the note-off at its start, for a tape-reverse feel. In ping-pong, Audio plays the endpoints twice, so every note gets one forward and one reversed pass.

Recording needs Forward direction. Bake and export freeze the direction into the notes and reset it to Forward.

12.2The DRUM LANE Bank

VideoTutorial 2.2: Euclidean rhythms and per-lane loops (from 1:39)

The DRUM LANE bank is the drum counterpart to the CLIP bank, acting on the selected lane only.

KnobWhat it doesRewrites notesDefault
1 · RESResolution. Alternate: ZOOM.Yes1/16
2 · STRCHStretch.Yes—
3 · SHIFTShift. Alternate: NUDGE.Yes0
4 · LGTOLegato, for this lane.Yes—
5 · EUCLDEuclid: spreads a number of hits evenly across the lane.Yes0
6 · CROPCrop, for this lane.Yes—
7 · DIRDirection. Alternate (REVRS): Reverse Style.NoFwd
8 · IMPRTImport MIDI.Yes—

Doubling with Stretch is refused with NOTES PAST THE LOOP END / CROP FIRST if hits lie past the loop's end.

Euclid keeps hand-placed hits on steps the pattern does not use. A hand-placed hit on a step the pattern lands on becomes part of it, and turning Euclid down removes it.

To set the lane's length, hold [Loop] and turn the jog. The lane's MIDI note is on the NOTE FX bank.

Zoom, Stretch, Shift and Legato need the lane's loop to start at step 1. Crop puts it there.

12.3The ALL LANES Bank

The ALL LANES bank applies one setting to all 32 lanes at once. [Loop] and the [Shift] + Step shortcuts also act on every lane while it is open.

KnobWhat it doesRewrites notes
1 · RESResolution for all lanes.Yes
2 · STRCHStretch all lanes.Yes
3 · SHIFTShift. Alternate: NUDGE.Yes
4 · QUANTQuantize all lanes at playback.No
5 · CROPCrop every lane.Yes
6 · INQNTRecording input quantize for the track.No
7 · DIRDirection for all lanes. Alternate (REVRS): Reverse Style.No
8 · RSYNCRepeat Sync: held repeats wait for the beat grid (On) or fire at once (Off).No

Stretch shows NO ROOM if any lane can't fit. Doubling is refused if hits lie past the loop's end; crop first. Stretch and Shift are refused with LOOP STARTS AFTER STEP 1 / CROP FIRST if any lane's loop starts later than step 1.

The track's velocity input, VelIn, is in TRACK CONFIG. You can also hold [Shift] and press [Step 10].

13

Sequencer Effects

VideoTutorial 4.5: The signal flow (from 6:25)

These effects work on notes before they reach the instrument. For audio effects such as reverb, see FX 1–4. There are two kinds:

  • Sequencer effects (NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY and SEQ ARP) reshape every note, sequenced or live, at playback, per clip. Return a knob to its default and the clip plays exactly as written.
  • Live input modifiers act only on what you play live, before it is sequenced. They are LIVE ARP on melodic tracks, and on drum tracks Note Repeat, shaped by RPT GROOVE.

Drum tracks have NOTE FX and DELAY only. Alternates work as on CLIP: touch the knob and click the jog, and press [Back] to switch back.

Everything runs as one chain, the live modifier first, then the effects:

A track's MIDI FX module comes before all of this. Set to Post, the default, it plays first and the effects work on what it plays. Set to Pre, it sits on what you play live, before LIVE ARP and before recording. See Position — Pre or Post in Editing a module.

The project's groove is applied after the chain. Performance Mode comes last.

13.1NOTE FX

VideoTutorial 4.1: NOTE FX and HARMONY

NOTE FX shifts every note's pitch, velocity, timing and length, on melodic and drum tracks.

KnobWhat it doesDefault
1 · OCTOctave shift (±4).0
2 · OFFSTNote offset, in scale degrees or semitones (±24).0
3 · VELVelocity offset (±127).0
4 · QUANTQuantize at playback (0–100 %).0 %
5 · LEN>Fixed note length in step-multiples (-- = as written).--
6 · GATEScales the length, 0–400 %.100 %
7Empty.
8 · RANDPitch randomness (0–24; -- at 0). Alternate (ALGO): Pure, Gaus or Walk.--

The ALGO choices set how RAND spreads its notes: Pure spreads them evenly, Gaus clusters them near the note, and Walk drifts from note to note.

On a drum track, knobs 1 and 2 (OCT, NOTE) set the selected lane's MIDI note. Knobs 3–6 apply to that lane, and 7–8 are empty.

13.1.1 Three Kinds of Quantize

  • INQNT, on CLIP and ALL LANES, snaps notes as you record them.
  • QUANT, here and on ALL LANES, pulls notes toward the grid as they play, and leaves the clip as written.
  • Holding [Shift] and pressing [Step 16] sets QUANT to 100 %.

13.2HARMONY

VideoTutorial 4.1: NOTE FX and HARMONY

HARMONY adds up to four voices to every note, on melodic tracks.

KnobWhat it does
OCTAn octave voice, ±4 octaves.
HARM1–HARM3Harmony intervals, ±24: scale degrees with Scale Aware on, semitones with it off.

A value of 0 turns that voice off. Negative values add the voice below the note.

13.3DELAY

VideoTutorial 4.2: MIDI DELAY (from 1:58)

DELAY echoes every note in rhythm, on melodic and drum tracks.

KnobWhat it doesDefault
1 · RATEDelay time, dotted and triplet values included. Alternate (CLKFB, ±100): Clock Feedback.1/8D
2 · LEVELEcho velocity.127
3 · REPTSNumber of echoes (0 = off).0
4 · VELFBVelocity change per repeat.0
5 · PITFBPitch change per repeat (scale-aware).0
6 · GATEFixed echo length (-- = natural).--
7 · RETRGA new note clears the echoes in flight.On
8 · RANDPitch randomness on echoes. Alternate (ALGO): Pure, Gaus or Walk.--

Clock Feedback makes each echo come sooner (negative values) or later (positive values) than the last, like a bouncing ball.

On a drum track DELAY has no pitch controls, and knobs 5–7 are Gate, Clock Feedback and Retrigger.

13.4SEQ ARP

VideoTutorial 4.3: SEQ ARP (from 3:21)

SEQ ARP is an arpeggiator that runs after DELAY, on both sequenced and live notes. It is on melodic tracks and is set per clip.

KnobWhat it doesDefault
1 · STYLEStyle: Up, Down, Up/Down, Converge, Diverge, Ordered, Random, and more.Off
2 · RATEArp rate.1/16
3 · OCTOctave range (±4). Negative values extend downward.Off
4 · GATENote length. Under 100 % shortens, over lengthens.100 %
5 · STEPSHow silenced steps behave: rest (Mute) or skip (Step).Mute
6 · RETRGRestarts the arp on each new note.On
7 · SYNCWaits for the next rate boundary.On

The extra octaves set by OCT join the notes the style orders. For example, Down with OCT at +1 plays from the top octave down.

13.4.1 The Arp Steps Editor

Each arp step can have its own pitch offset and velocity. To open the per-step editor, touch knob 5 (STEPS) and click the jog. It works the same on LIVE ARP.

  • Knobs 1–8 set each step's pitch offset (±24 scale degrees). With [Shift] held, they set each step's velocity. Thru passes the incoming velocity.
  • On the pads, the column is the step and the row is one of four velocity levels, bottom to top. Press the bottom row again to turn the step off. Hold [Delete] and tap a pad to set Thru.
  • To set the step-loop length (1–8), hold [Loop] and tap a pad.

To close the editor, turn the jog or press [Back].

13.5Live Input Modifiers

Live input modifiers shape what you play live, on the pads or over external MIDI, before it is sequenced. The stored clip is left untouched.

13.5.1 LIVE ARP

VideoTutorial 4.4: LIVE ARP (from 5:09)

LIVE ARP arpeggiates live pad and external input only, on melodic tracks and Slicers. It is set per track, not per clip.

The controls match SEQ ARP, except that Retrigger defaults to Off. Knob 8 adds Latch (LATCH), which keeps the arp running after you let go of the pads.

  • To latch, press [Loop] while holding pads. Press [Loop] again with pads held to unlatch.
  • Press [Loop] with no pads held to clear the latched notes. Latch stays on.
  • Stop, [Delete] + [Play], or switching to Session View unlatches.

On Slicer and Audio tracks, Step replaces Oct; see Slicer track banks.

To turn LIVE ARP on or off with the last style, hold [Shift] and press [Step 11].

To open LIVE ARP's page, hold [Shift] and hold [Step 11] for about half a second; press [Back] to close it. LIVE ARP is an ordinary bank: the knobs stay on it after the page closes, and it is the second pad of the IN column on the bank map.

LIVE ARP can't be automated, because its settings belong to the track rather than a clip. It is still available as a macro destination.

13.5.2 RPT GROOVE

Repeat Groove shapes the 8-step gate mask of a drum lane's Note Repeat. It is set per lane, and you hear it while a repeat mode is active.

RPT GROOVE has two pages. To switch pages, touch any knob and click the jog.

KnobVelocity pageNudge page
1–8Velocity per gate step: Thru (the pad's own velocity) or a value 1–127Nudge per gate step (±50 % of the step)

To reset the selected lane's groove, hold [Delete] and click the jog, even with no repeat mode on.

14

Automation

VideoTutorial 6.2: Automation (from 1:22) · Tutorial 6.3: Automating sounds and effects (from 4:08)

Almost anything you can turn in dAVEBOx, you can automate: a Schwung instrument's or effect's parameter, a level, a bank knob, or a MIDI target. There is no lane to arm. The knob that plays a parameter records it.

A Move instrument's own parameters can't be automated. On a track that plays one of Move's instruments, such as Drift, Wavetable or a drum rack, dAVEBOx can't reach those knobs: holding a step and turning one writes no lock, and recording doesn't capture it. The track's levels, its MACROS (Aftertouch, Pitch Bend) and dAVEBOx's own bank knobs still automate there.

14.1Making It

There are two ways to make automation: record it, or lock a step.

14.1.1 Recording It

With the transport playing and [Record] armed, turn a knob. The move is written at the playhead for as long as your hand is on the knob, round the loop as many times as you hold it. See Recording.

Each time you start, a notice gives the length of the lane you are recording onto, for example ● LANE: 2 BAR, or ● LANE: 13 ST when it isn't whole bars. The move repeats on that cycle.

14.1.2 Locking a Step

To lock a step, hold the step and turn a knob. The step takes a lock, also called a punch: the value is held flat for the whole step. The parameter jumps to it as the step starts, and jumps back to what the lane was doing when the step ends. To stretch the lock across several steps, press a later step while you hold; see Editing a Lane on the Steps. See also Editing notes.

To place a point instead, tap [Shift] while you hold the step, before or after turning. The step gets a single point, which the lane glides into and on from. Tap [Shift] again for PUNCH. Every hold starts as a punch. Holding [Shift] while you turn is still fine adjustment.

While you hold a step, every automated parameter on screen shows the value it plays at that step, until you let go.

To remove the automation on a step, on every lane, hold [Delete] and press the step. Deleting a punch gives the lane back as it was before it.

14.1.3 How a Lane Plays

Each lane is one envelope. Its points glide into each other, and a lock is where it jumps. Parameters that are a choice or a switch step from value to value instead.

A lane starts where its parameter rests: its first point also puts one on the lane's first step, carrying the resting value. At the end of the loop the lane does what its Wrap says; see Lane Operations.

The resting value is where a parameter sits when nothing automates it: on Stop, and in clips without automation for it. There is one per parameter on its track. Turn the knob while stopped, or while a clip with no automation for it is playing, and that becomes the new resting value. While the playing clip does automate it, turning the knob without [Record] takes the parameter over until you let go.

Switching clips returns the old clip's automated parameters to rest. A clip that automates the same parameter starts where its own lane starts, straight away. A parameter whose automation you muted stays where you put it.

14.1.4 What Can Be Automated

  • A Schwung module's editor pages.
  • The levels on MIX and in the session mixer.
  • The eight MACROS.
